# AccessContextManagerAuthorizedOrgsDesc

`accesscontextmanager.gcp.hfl.dev/v1alpha1`

**Gap it fills.** Terraform's `google_access_context_manager_authorized_orgs_desc`. The organizations an organization's access policy trusts for, or lets evaluate, device and credential strength signals; accessPolicy is the access policy's number. The ID starts with a letter, then letters, digits or _.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the accesscontextmanager.v1 Discovery document; fixtures, field names and immutable fields copied from Config Connector's open pull request #14202 (a Terraform-based kind there; `UPSTREAM.md`, `docs/design.md` section 2.3).

## Notes

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` (`docs/design.md`
section 2.4); its test is `pkg/discokind/kindtest` with the fixtures under
`pkg/controller/direct/accesscontextmanager/discokindtest/testdata/discokind/AccessContextManagerAuthorizedOrgsDesc/`.

2026-11-23: built (foundation item 21). `spec.accessPolicy` is the
access policy's number (Config Connector's pull request names it by
`accessPolicyRef`); `assetType`, `authorizationDirection` and
`authorizationType` are immutable (Terraform's resource and the pull
request say so; the API's patch changes `orgs`). The API's create takes
no ID parameter: the full name goes in the body (`nameInBody`, which now
covers a create with no ID parameter). The ID must start with a letter,
then letters, digits or `_`, so the fixtures use `${ID}`. When #14202 is
released, objects move to Config Connector's kind as `docs/design.md`
section 2.3 says. Live: pending (`live-skip`: it needs an organization's
access policy and Access Context Manager roles on it, and a live run
never touches the organization); with them, `task test-live
PROJECT=$GCP_PROJECT KINDS=accesscontextmanager` once `live-skip` is
lifted, the access policy in the fixtures set, and the sweeper taught to
delete the run's descriptions.
